verdict.headline: Stocks end the week near a record as bank results and inflation data come next
verdict.label: Weekend: S&P 500 closed Fri at 7,811.54 (+0.59%, week about +1.1%), 7 pts under its 7,818.93 record; Nasdaq 27,366.17 (week about +0.6%); 10Y ~5.24% (week about -4 to -5 bp, Wed high 5.331%), 30Y ~5.60%; Brent ~$103-104; BTC ~$82,780 Sat; Dec hike odds ~69%.
verdict.horizon: four trading sessions, Tuesday October 13 through Friday October 16 (bond market shut Monday for Columbus Day)
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: the S&P 500 rose about 1.1% over the week, going by Friday's close of 7,811.54 against the prior Friday's 7,722.72, and ended 7 points under its October 6 record. That came through a rough patch: Thursday's report that OpenAI's revenue was lower than estimated hit AI stocks, and Friday's SpaceX spectrum deal sent Verizon, AT&T and T-Mobile down 9% to 13%. The ten-year yield ended near 5.24%, about 4 to 5 basis points lower on the week, after touching 5.331% on Wednesday, its highest since 2002. Brent ended near $103-104, still above $100 with the Strait of Hormuz closed. Bitcoin is near $82,780 on Saturday, little changed in 24 hours.

What it means: stocks absorbed a sector-specific shock, a hit to the AI story and long yields at 2002 highs, and still finished the week up. That shows resilience, but it also means the index goes into earnings season priced close to its best level, with less room for disappointment. The evidence points both ways: bond buyers took more than 72% of Friday's 30-year auction as indirect bidders, a sign of demand at these yields, while futures markets still price about a 69% chance of a December rate hike, a sign inflation worry has not gone away. Which side wins is not settled by this week.

What would change the picture: September CPI on Wednesday, October 14, forecast at about 3.6-3.7% for the year from 3.4%, is the first full month of oil above $100 and the last inflation report before the Fed's October 28 decision. A core reading above forecast would likely push the ten-year back toward 5.331%; a soft one would ease pressure on stocks near their record. Bank results from Tuesday show whether borrowers and spending are holding up under these rates. An S&P 500 close above 7,818.93 would be a new record; a close under 7,666.45 would show the week's weakness spreading. This read is lower-conviction than usual: it is a weekend, no stock or bond market has traded since Friday, news sites could not be opened from this run so figures rest on search summaries of the cited sources, sources disagree on the week's percentage gains and on Friday's oil settlement, and VIX and dollar-index closes were unavailable.
verdict.lede_short: The S&P 500 rose about 1.1% this week to within 7 points of its record despite an AI revenue scare, a telecom selloff and ten-year yields touching 5.331%, their highest since 2002. That leaves stocks priced near their best going into bank results from Tuesday and September CPI on Wednesday, forecast at 3.6-3.7% with oil above $100. A hot core reading would test the bond-yield highs again; a soft one would ease the main pressure on stocks.

supporting_data.label: The S&P 500 closed Friday at 7,811.54, up 0.59% on the day and about 1.1% on the week, 7 points under its October 6 record — stocks finished higher through a week of sector shocks, so the index enters earnings season near its peak.

September CPI is due Wednesday, October 14, with headline inflation forecast at about 3.6-3.7% from 3.4% — it is the first full month of oil above $100 and the last inflation report before the Fed's October 28 decision.
The ten-year yield ended near 5.24%, about 4 to 5 basis points lower on the week, after touching 5.331% on Wednesday — long-term borrowing costs eased but remain close to their highest since 2002.

Indirect bidders, a group that includes foreign central banks, took more than 72% of Friday's $22 billion 30-year bond sale — buyers are showing up at these yields, which argues against a disorderly rise.

JPMorgan, Wells Fargo and Citigroup are scheduled to report on Tuesday, October 13, with Bank of America on CPI morning — their loan losses and consumer spending data are the first broad check on how households are handling high rates and $4 gasoline.

Brent ended Friday near $103-104 after President Trump said the US will not strike Iran before the November 3 midterms — the pledge eased fears of escalation but the Strait of Hormuz remains closed, so oil stays above $100.

Bitcoin traded near $82,780 on Saturday morning, little changed over 24 hours in a $82,214-83,253 range — it is holding above Thursday's $80,320 low with no weekend move to signal a shift in risk appetite.
